analysis:
All three changed files are test-only (SSDCheckpointMaintenanceEpochTests, SSDCheckpointRecencyCoordinationTests, SSDHybridCheckpointCoordinationTests) under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/. No production source, endpoints, key handling, or crypto code changes in the supplied evidence, so there is no direct regression against T-041 or TB-007.

The tests document an intended production design change in the encrypted SSD prefix-cache file coordinator (SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator). Readers take a shared-mode lease. Recency touches and publication need a shared-to-exclusive upgrade (tryUpgrade/downgrade), which succeeds only when the reader is alone. Duplicate validation by a donation writer is exclusive and queues ahead of later readers. Retirement, eviction and scans skip files a reader holds. A corrupt file is removed only by a sole reader. TTL retirement now consults the loaded store's own last-hit (index.touch) before removal.

These behaviours assert that authenticated-read snapshot integrity (AEAD plus file identity matching) is preserved, and that corruption detection and tamper-to-delete still work. The tests do not weaken authentication: authenticationIsNotRelaxed is unchanged and external replacement and ciphertext corruption are still rejected. They also keep the epoch stable across single-file eviction and TTL removal, which matches the T-041 note that the epoch is a routing-evidence generation and not a purge primitive.

Open integration questions for the next pass: the production coordinator, store and maintainer implementations are not in this batch, so the shared-to-exclusive upgrade, writer-priority queueing and TTL sweep consulting the in-memory last-hit cannot be verified. In particular, I cannot confirm that the TTL purge still bounds at-rest retention (30-minute sliding TTL) if a held or recently hit file is skipped, or that a persistent reader cannot starve TTL, budget or retirement. That bounded-retention behaviour is part of the T-041 mitigation. No finding is raised because there is no visible production change.
